const allTracks = [
  ...instrumentals.map(([title, type, prompt], index) => ({ index, title, type, prompt, mode: "Instrumental" })),
  ...songs.map(([title, type, prompt, lyrics], index) => ({ index: index + 20, title, type, prompt, lyrics, mode: "Song" })),
];

function slugify(value) {
  return value.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, "-").replace(/^-|-$/g, "");
}

async function generate(track) {
  const slug = `${String(track.index + 1).padStart(2, "0")}-${slugify(track.title)}`;
  const audioPath = path.join(outDir, `${slug}.mp3`);
  try {
    await fs.access(audioPath);
    console.log(`skip ${track.title}`);
    return { ...track, file: `seed_music/${slug}.mp3` };
  } catch {}

  const body = {
    model: "music-2.6",
    prompt: track.prompt,
    is_instrumental: track.type === "instrumental",
    output_format: "url",
    audio_setting: audioSetting,
  };
  if (track.type === "song") {
    body.lyrics = track.lyrics;
    body.lyrics_optimizer = false;
  }

  console.log(`generate ${track.index + 1}/40 ${track.title}`);
  const res = await fetch("https://api.minimax.io/v1/music_generation", {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${apiKey}`,
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
  });
  const text = await res.text();
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`request failed ${res.status}: ${text}`);
  const json = JSON.parse(text);
  if (json.base_resp?.status_code !== 0) {
    throw new Error(`generation failed: ${json.base_resp?.status_msg || text}`);
  }
  const audioUrl = json.data?.audio;
  if (!audioUrl?.startsWith("http")) throw new Error(`missing audio url: ${text}`);
  const audioRes = await fetch(audioUrl);
  if (!audioRes.ok) throw new Error(`download failed ${audioRes.status}`);
  const bytes = Buffer.from(await audioRes.arrayBuffer());
  await fs.writeFile(audioPath, bytes);
  return {
    ...track,
    file: `seed_music/${slug}.mp3`,
    durationMs: json.extra_info?.music_duration || null,
  };
}

const manifest = [];
for (const track of allTracks) {
  const entry = await generate(track);
  manifest.push({
    title: entry.title,
    mode: entry.mode,
    prompt: entry.prompt,
    file: entry.file,
    durationMs: entry.durationMs || null,
  });
  await fs.writeFile(path.join(outDir, "manifest.json"), JSON.stringify(manifest, null, 2));
}

console.log(`wrote ${manifest.length} tracks to ${outDir}`);

<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, call `load_workspace_dependencies` to find the bundled runtime and libraries.
- If workspace dependencies are missing, call `install_workspace_dependencies` first.

### Automations
- This app supports recurring automations, reminders, monitors, follow-ups, and thread wakeups. When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.
- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}
</app-context>

<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, call `load_workspace_dependencies` to find the bundled runtime and libraries.
- If workspace dependencies are missing, call `install_workspace_dependencies` first.

### Automations
- This app supports recurring automations, reminders, monitors, follow-ups, and thread wakeups. When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.
- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}
</app-context>

# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, call `load_workspace_dependencies` to find the bundled runtime and libraries.
- If workspace dependencies are missing, call `install_workspace_dependencies` first.

### Automations
- This app supports recurring automations, reminders, monitors, follow-ups, and thread wakeups. When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.
- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}

The `request_user_input` tool is unavailable in Default mode. If you call it while in Default mode, it will return an error.

<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, call `load_workspace_dependencies` to find the bundled runtime and libraries.
- If workspace dependencies are missing, call `install_workspace_dependencies` first.

### Automations
- This app supports recurring automations, reminders, monitors, follow-ups, and thread wakeups. When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.
- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}
</app-context>

@Composable
fun FlashPlayAndroidApp(store: FlashPlayViewModel) {
    val tracks = store.feedTracks
    var activeTrackId by remember { mutableStateOf<String?>(null) }
    var player by remember { mutableStateOf<MediaPlayer?>(null) }
    var playbackError by remember { mutableStateOf<String?>(null) }

    fun stopPlayback() {
        player?.runCatching {
            stop()
            release()
        }
        player = null
        activeTrackId = null
    }

    fun playTrack(track: MusicTrack) {
        if (activeTrackId == track.id) {
            stopPlayback()
            return
        }
        playbackError = null
        stopPlayback()
        val nextPlayer = MediaPlayer().apply {
            setAudioAttributes(
                AudioAttributes.Builder()
                    .setUsage(AudioAttributes.USAGE_MEDIA)
                    .setContentType(AudioAttributes.CONTENT_TYPE_MUSIC)
                    .build()
            )
            val localFile = File(track.localPath)
            setDataSource(if (localFile.exists()) localFile.absolutePath else track.audioUrl)
            setOnPreparedListener {
                it.start()
                activeTrackId = track.id
            }
            setOnCompletionListener { stopPlayback() }
            setOnErrorListener { _, _, _ ->
                playbackError = "Playback failed. The local music file may be unavailable."
                stopPlayback()
                true
            }
            prepareAsync()
        }
        player = nextPlayer
    }

    DisposableEffect(Unit) {
        onDispose { stopPlayback() }
    }

    LaunchedEffect(store.pendingPlayTrackId, tracks) {
        val pending = store.pendingPlayTrackId ?: return@LaunchedEffect
        tracks.firstOrNull { it.id == pending }?.let(::playTrack)
        store.consumePendingPlayTrackId()
    }

    MaterialTheme {
        Box(
            modifier = Modifier
                .fillMaxSize()

# Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

The `request_user_input` tool is unavailable in Default mode. If you call it while in Default mode, it will return an error.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions. If you absolutely must ask a question because the answer cannot be discovered from local context and a reasonable assumption would be risky, ask the user directly with a concise plain-text question. Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.

payload.developer_instructions:
<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, call `load_workspace_dependencies` to find the bundled runtime and libraries.
- If workspace dependencies are missing, call `install_workspace_dependencies` first.

### Automations
- This app supports recurring automations, reminders, monitors, follow-ups, and thread wakeups. When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.
- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}
</app-context>

fun FlashPlayAndroidApp(store: FlashPlayViewModel) {
    val tracks = store.feedTracks
    var activeTrackId by remember { mutableStateOf<String?>(null) }
    var player by remember { mutableStateOf<MediaPlayer?>(null) }
    var playbackError by remember { mutableStateOf<String?>(null) }

    fun stopPlayback() {
        player?.runCatching {
            stop()
            release()
        }
        player = null
        activeTrackId = null
    }

    fun playTrack(track: MusicTrack) {
        if (activeTrackId == track.id) {
            stopPlayback()
            return
        }
        playbackError = null
        stopPlayback()
        val nextPlayer = MediaPlayer().apply {
            setAudioAttributes(
                AudioAttributes.Builder()
                    .setUsage(AudioAttributes.USAGE_MEDIA)
                    .setContentType(AudioAttributes.CONTENT_TYPE_MUSIC)
                    .build()
            )
            val localFile = File(track.localPath)
            setDataSource(if (localFile.exists()) localFile.absolutePath else track.audioUrl)
            setOnPreparedListener {
                it.start()
                activeTrackId = track.id
            }
            setOnCompletionListener { stopPlayback() }
            setOnErrorListener { _, _, _ ->
                playbackError = "Playback failed. The local music file may be unavailable."
                stopPlayback()
                true
            }
            prepareAsync()
        }
        player = nextPlayer
    }

    DisposableEffect(Unit) {
        onDispose { stopPlayback() }
    }

    LaunchedEffect(store.pendingPlayTrackId, tracks) {
        val pending = store.pendingPlayTrackId ?: return@LaunchedEffect
        tracks.firstOrNull { it.id == pending }?.let(::playTrack)
        store.consumePendingPlayTrackId()
    }

    MaterialTheme {
        Box(
            modifier = Modifier
                .fillMaxSize()
                .background(FlashPlayPalette.Background)
        ) {
            when (store.selectedTab) {
                FlashTab.Home -> ListenScreen(
                    dailyVibe = store.dailyVibe,
                    tracks = tracks,
                    activeTrackId = activeTrackId,
                    playbackError = playbackError,
                    onPlay = ::playTrack,
                    onFavorite = store::toggleFavorite
                )
                FlashTab.Create -> CreateScreen(store = store)
                FlashTab.Agent -> AgentScreen(store = store)
                FlashTab.Me -> LibraryScreen(
                    generatedTracks = store.generatedTracks,
                    favoriteTracks = store.favoriteTracks,
                    activeTrackId = activeTrackId,
                    onOpen = store::openTrack,
                    onPlay = ::playTrack
                )
            }

            BottomBar(
                selectedTab = store.selectedTab,
                onSelect = store::switchTab,
                modifier = Modifier.align(Alignment.BottomCenter)
            )
        }
    }
}

# Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

The `request_user_input` tool is unavailable in Default mode. If you call it while in Default mode, it will return an error.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions. If you absolutely must ask a question because the answer cannot be discovered from local context and a reasonable assumption would be risky, ask the user directly with a concise plain-text question. Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.

<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, call `load_workspace_dependencies` to find the bundled runtime and libraries.
- If workspace dependencies are missing, call `install_workspace_dependencies` first.

### Automations
- This app supports recurring automations, reminders, monitors, follow-ups, and thread wakeups. When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.

### Review findings

已重新构建并安装成功，APK 路径仍是：

`/Users/vincet/Desktop/aigame2/android/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk`

# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, call `load_workspace_dependencies` to find the bundled runtime and libraries.
- If workspace dependencies are missing, call `install_workspace_dependencies` first.

### Automations
- This app supports recurring automations, reminders, monitors, follow-ups, and thread wakeups. When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.
- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}
</app-context>

# Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

The `request_user_input` tool is unavailable in Default mode. If you call it while in Default mode, it will return an error.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions. If you absolutely must ask a question because the answer cannot be discovered from local context and a reasonable assumption would be risky, ask the user directly with a concise plain-text question. Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.

<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, call `load_workspace_dependencies` to find the bundled runtime and libraries.
- If workspace dependencies are missing, call `install_workspace_dependencies` first.

### Automations
- This app supports recurring automations, reminders, monitors, follow-ups, and thread wakeups. When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.
- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}
</app-context>

- compositing — multi-image insert/merge with matched lighting/perspective.
- sketch-to-render — drawing/line art to photoreal render.

Use case: <taxonomy slug>
Asset type: <where the asset will be used>
Primary request: <user's main prompt>

Scene/backdrop: <environment>

package com.museplay.android

import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Color
import java.util.UUID

enum class FlashTab(val label: String) {
    Home("Listen"),
    Create("Create"),
    Agent("Agent"),
    Me("Library")
}

enum class MusicMode(
    val label: String,
    val isInstrumental: Boolean
) {
    Instrumental("Instrumental", true),
    Song("Song", false)
}

data class MusicPalette(
    val accent: Color,
    val primary: Color,
    val secondary: Color
)

data class MusicTrack(
    val id: String = UUID.randomUUID().toString(),
    val title: String,
    val summary: String,
    val prompt: String,
    val audioUrl: String,
    val localPath: String,
    val durationMs: Long?,
    val mode: MusicMode,
    val palette: MusicPalette,
    val creator: String,
    val isGenerated: Boolean = false,
    val isFavorite: Boolean = false
)

data class GeneratedMusic(
    val title: String,
    val summary: String,
    val prompt: String,
    val audioUrl: String,
    val localPath: String,
    val durationMs: Long?,
    val mode: MusicMode,
    val model: String
)

data class AgentMessage(
    val text: String,
    val fromUser: Boolean,
    val mood: String = "Neutral",
    val expression: String = "calm",
    val createdAt: Long = System.currentTimeMillis()
)

data class MusicRecommendation(
    val title: String,
    val mood: String,
    val prompt: String
)

data class EmotionInsight(
    val mood: String,
    val energy: String,
    val musicDirection: String
)

object FlashPlayPalette {
    val Background = Color(0xFFF6F8FA)
    val Surface = Color.White
    val Ink = Color(0xFF111827)
    val Brand = Color(0xFF0E7C66)
    val Warm = Color(0xFFFFD166)
    val Mist = Color(0xFFE7F4EF)

    val Cards = listOf(
        MusicPalette(Color(0xFF0E7C66), Color(0xFFC7F3E5), Color(0xFFF8E7A1)),
        MusicPalette(Color(0xFFEF476F), Color(0xFFFFD0DC), Color(0xFFE7F0FF)),
        MusicPalette(Color(0xFF118AB2), Color(0xFFCDEFFF), Color(0xFFEAF7C9)),
        MusicPalette(Color(0xFF6D5DFB), Color(0xFFDCD8FF), Color(0xFFFFE0B8)),
        MusicPalette(Color(0xFFB85C38), Color(0xFFFFD8C2), Color(0xFFDDF4FF))
    )
}

object SampleMusic {
    fun feed(): List<MusicTrack> = emptyList()
}

fun MusicTrack.toJson(): org.json.JSONObject = org.json.JSONObject().apply {
    put("id", id)
    put("title", title)
    put("summary", summary)
    put("prompt", prompt)
    put("audioUrl", audioUrl)
    put("localPath", localPath)
    put("durationMs", durationMs ?: org.json.JSONObject.NULL)
    put("mode", mode.name)
    put("creator", creator)
    put("isGenerated", isGenerated)
    put("isFavorite", isFavorite)
}

fun AgentMessage.toJson(): org.json.JSONObject = org.json.JSONObject().apply {
    put("text", text)
    put("fromUser", fromUser)
    put("mood", mood)
    put("expression", expression)
    put("createdAt", createdAt)
}

fun agentMessageFromJson(json: org.json.JSONObject): AgentMessage {
    return AgentMessage(
        text = json.optString("text"),
        fromUser = json.optBoolean("fromUser"),
        mood = json.optString("mood", "Neutral"),
        expression = json.optString("expression", "calm"),
        createdAt = json.optLong("createdAt", System.currentTimeMillis())
    )
}

fun musicTrackFromJson(json: org.json.JSONObject, palette: MusicPalette): MusicTrack {
    return MusicTrack(
        id = json.optString("id").ifBlank { UUID.randomUUID().toString() },
        title = json.optString("title", "Generated Track"),
        summary = json.optString("summary", "Generated and saved locally."),
        prompt = json.optString("prompt"),
        audioUrl = json.optString("audioUrl"),
        localPath = json.optString("localPath"),
        durationMs = json.optLong("durationMs").takeIf { !json.isNull("durationMs") && it > 0 },
        mode = runCatching { MusicMode.valueOf(json.optString("mode")) }.getOrDefault(MusicMode.Instrumental),
        palette = palette,
        creator = json.optString("creator", "Local"),
        isGenerated = json.optBoolean("isGenerated", true),
        isFavorite = json.optBoolean("isFavorite", false)
    )
}

fun MusicTrack.toJson(): org.json.JSONObject = org.json.JSONObject().apply {
    put("id", id)
    put("title", title)
    put("summary", summary)
    put("prompt", prompt)
    put("audioUrl", audioUrl)
    put("localPath", localPath)
    put("durationMs", durationMs ?: org.json.JSONObject.NULL)
    put("mode", mode.name)
    put("creator", creator)
    put("isGenerated", isGenerated)
    put("isFavorite", isFavorite)
}

fun AgentMessage.toJson(): org.json.JSONObject = org.json.JSONObject().apply {
    put("text", text)
    put("fromUser", fromUser)
    put("mood", mood)
    put("expression", expression)
    put("createdAt", createdAt)
}

fun agentMessageFromJson(json: org.json.JSONObject): AgentMessage {
    return AgentMessage(
        text = json.optString("text"),
        fromUser = json.optBoolean("fromUser"),
        mood = json.optString("mood", "Neutral"),
        expression = json.optString("expression", "calm"),
        createdAt = json.optLong("createdAt", System.currentTimeMillis())
    )
}

fun musicTrackFromJson(json: org.json.JSONObject, palette: MusicPalette): MusicTrack {
    return MusicTrack(
        id = json.optString("id").ifBlank { UUID.randomUUID().toString() },
        title = json.optString("title", "Generated Track"),
        summary = json.optString("summary", "Generated and saved locally."),
        prompt = json.optString("prompt"),
        audioUrl = json.optString("audioUrl"),
        localPath = json.optString("localPath"),
        durationMs = json.optLong("durationMs").takeIf { !json.isNull("durationMs") && it > 0 },
        mode = runCatching { MusicMode.valueOf(json.optString("mode")) }.getOrDefault(MusicMode.Instrumental),
        palette = palette,
        creator = json.optString("creator", "Local"),
        isGenerated = json.optBoolean("isGenerated", true),
        isFavorite = json.optBoolean("isFavorite", false)
    )
}

- This app supports recurring automations, reminders, monitors, follow-ups, and thread wakeups. When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).

- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.

已完成第一版。

我搜索了 LottieFiles，但它的下载页对 CLI 有 Cloudflare 防护，无法直接批量抓 JSON。为了让功能先完整落地，我在 APK 内置了 6 个标准 Lottie JSON 音乐动画，风格包括：均衡器、电波轨道、唱片旋转、漂浮粒子、声波堆叠、柔和音量柱。

已实现：

- Feed 页面中间的旧静态波形已替换为 Lottie 动画展示区。
- Lottie 动画库存储在 APK 内：`/Users/vincet/Desktop/aigame2/android/app/src/main/assets/lottie_music/`
- 每首音乐会根据 `track.id` 随机但稳定匹配一个动画。
- 播放时动画循环，暂停时动画停止在当前进度。
- 已加入 `lottie-compose:6.7.1` 并构建成功。
- 已安装到模拟器测试，Feed 页面正常显示，旧截图中的静态波形内容已被替换。

新版 APK：

`/Users/vincet/Desktop/aigame2/android/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk`

<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, call `load_workspace_dependencies` to find the bundled runtime and libraries.
- If workspace dependencies are missing, call `install_workspace_dependencies` first.

### Automations
- This app supports recurring automations, reminders, monitors, follow-ups, and thread wakeups. When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.
- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}
</app-context>

content.text: 如何获得优质的LottieFiles动画库；目前几个动画不够优质

payload.message: 如何获得优质的LottieFiles动画库；目前几个动画不够优质

可以，当前这几个只是“本地兜底动画”，质量确实不够像成品音乐 App。要获得优质 LottieFiles 动画库，建议走这几条路线：

**最佳方案**
购买或订阅 LottieFiles 高质量动画，然后手动下载 `.json` / `.lottie` 文件，放进 APK 的 `assets/lottie_music/`。  
LottieFiles 网页有 Cloudflare，脚本批量抓取不稳定，也不适合绕过。最稳的是在浏览器登录账号后下载授权文件。

**选动画标准**
优先选这些关键词：

- `music visualizer`
- `equalizer`
- `sound wave`
- `vinyl`
- `audio spectrum`
- `music player`
- `dj`
- `ambient particles`
- `abstract loop`
- `sound pulse`

挑选时看这几个指标：

- 必须是 loop 动画
- 背景透明或纯色可融合
- 不要太复杂，单个 JSON 最好小于 300KB
- 风格统一，避免一首歌像卡通、一首歌像商务插画
- 适合竖屏中间展示，不要横向太宽
- 授权允许 App 内商用分发

**落地做法**
把下载的文件命名成这样：

```text
android/app/src/main/assets/lottie_music/
  equalizer_neon.json
  vinyl_gold.json
  ambient_particles.json
  sound_wave_soft.json
  pulse_orbit.json
  synth_loop.json
```

然后更新：

```text
android/app/src/main/assets/lottie_music/manifest.json
```

我可以继续帮你做一个“高质量动画库接入器”：你只要把下载好的 Lottie 文件丢进文件夹，我自动扫描、生成 manifest、按音乐风格匹配动画，并在 App 里做预览。

payload.message:
我搜了 `uiverse-io/galaxy`。结论：它是 Uiverse 的开源 UI 库镜像，主要是 **HTML/CSS/Tailwind**，不是 Android 原生组件，所以不能直接复制进 APK，但很多动效可以用 Compose 复刻。repo 里有 Buttons、Cards、Inputs、Notifications、Patterns、loaders 等分类，并且 MIT 许可，可改造使用。来源：[uiverse-io/galaxy](https://github.com/uiverse-io/galaxy)。

适合本 App 的优先级：

1. **loaders**
最适合。可用于 `Generate music` 生成中状态、Agent 思考中、音乐上传/下载等待态。建议复刻成音乐频谱、旋转唱片、脉冲圆环，比现在普通 loading 更像音乐产品。

2. **Buttons**
适合替换当前 `Generate music`、`Shuffle`、Agent 发送按钮。可做发光边框、按压弹性、液态 hover 的移动端版本，但不要太花，保留极简。

3. **Cards**
适合 Library 里的音乐卡片、Agent 推荐音乐卡片、Create 页 Prompt bank 卡片。可以借鉴玻璃拟态、渐变边框、hover lift，但 Compose 里要改成 tap/press 动效。

4. **Toggle-switches / Radio-buttons**
适合 `Instrumental / Song` 模式切换。现在 FilterChip 比较普通，可以改成更有质感的 segmented control。

5. **Inputs / Forms**
适合 Create 页的 Track title 和 Music prompt 输入框。可以做 focus 发光边框、浮动 label、轻微 scale，但不建议使用太复杂的网页输入框效果。

6. **Notifications**
适合生成成功、失败、保存本地、API 错误的 Toast/Notice。可以做滑入、弹性、颜色分级。

不建议优先用：

- **Patterns**：大多是背景装饰，容易让音乐 feed 变乱。
- **Checkboxes**：当前 App 不太需要。
- 复杂 CSS 3D 卡片：Android Compose 复刻成本高，性能也未必好。

我的建议：先把 `loaders + buttons + mode toggle + notice` 四类做进 App，收益最大。它们能直接改善“生成音乐等待、点击手感、创建页质感、错误反馈”。

# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, call `load_workspace_dependencies` to find the bundled runtime and libraries.
- If workspace dependencies are missing, call `install_workspace_dependencies` first.

### Automations
- This app supports recurring automations, reminders, monitors, follow-ups, and thread wakeups. When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.
- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}

+private fun GalaxyModeToggle(
+    selectedMode: MusicMode,
+    onSelect: (MusicMode) -> Unit
+) {
+    Surface(
+        modifier = Modifier
+            .fillMaxWidth()
+            .border(1.dp, Color.White.copy(alpha = 0.86f), RoundedCornerShape(22.dp)),
+        shape = RoundedCornerShape(22.dp),
+        color = FlashPlayPalette.Ink.copy(alpha = 0.06f)
+    ) {
+        Row(
+            modifier = Modifier.padding(5.dp),
+            horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(6.dp)
+        ) {
+            MusicMode.entries.forEach { mode ->
+                val selected = selectedMode == mode
+                val interactionSource = remember { MutableInteractionSource() }
+                val pressed by interactionSource.collectIsPressedAsState()
+                val scale by animateFloatAsState(
+                    targetValue = if (pressed) 0.96f else 1f,
+                    animationSpec = spring(stiffness = Spring.StiffnessMediumLow, dampingRatio = Spring.DampingRatioMediumBouncy),
+                    label = "mode-scale"
+                )
+                val bg by animateColorAsState(
+                    targetValue = if (selected) FlashPlayPalette.Ink else Color.White.copy(alpha = 0.72f),
+                    animationSpec = tween(180),
+                    label = "mode-bg"
+                )
+                val fg by animateColorAsState(
+                    targetValue = if (selected) Color.White else FlashPlayPalette.Ink,
+                    animationSpec = tween(180),
+                    label = "mode-fg"
+                )
+                Box(
+                    modifier = Modifier
+                        .weight(1f)
+                        .height(48.dp)
+                        .graphicsLayer {
+                            scaleX = scale
+                            scaleY = scale
+                        }
+                        .clip(RoundedCornerShape(17.dp))
+                        .background(bg)
+                        .clickable(
+                            interactionSource = interactionSource,
+                            indication = LocalIndication.current
+                        ) { onSelect(mode) },
+                    contentAlignment = Alignment.Center
+                ) {
+                    Text(mode.label, color = fg, fontWeight = FontWeight.Black, fontSize = 14.sp)
+                }
+            }
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+@Composable
+private fun GalaxyGenerateButton(
+    isGenerating: Boolean,
+    onClick: () -> Unit
+) {
+    val interactionSource = remember { MutableInteractionSource() }
+    val pressed by interactionSource.collectIsPressedAsState()
+    val pulse = rememberInfiniteTransition(label = "generate-pulse")
+    val phase by pulse.animateFloat(
+        initialValue = 0f,
+        targetValue = 1f,
+        animationSpec = infiniteRepeatable(animation = tween(1500), repeatMode = RepeatMode.Restart),
+        label = "generate-phase"
+    )
+    val scale by animateFloatAsState(
+        targetValue = if (pressed) 0.975f else 1f,
+        animationSpec = spring(stiffness = Spring.StiffnessMediumLow, dampingRatio = Spring.DampingRatioMediumBouncy),
+        label = "generate-scale"
+    )
+    val gradient = Brush.linearGradient(
+        colors = listOf(
+            FlashPlayPalette.Brand,
+            Color(0xFF22C6A3),
+            FlashPlayPalette.Warm,
+            FlashPlayPalette.Brand
+        ),
+        start = Offset(phase * 900f - 320f, 0f),
+        end = Offset(phase * 900f, 260f)
+    )
+
+    Box(
+        modifier = Modifier
+            .fillMaxWidth()
+            .height(62.dp)
+            .graphicsLayer {
+                scaleX = scale
+                scaleY = scale
+            }
+            .clip(RoundedCornerShape(20.dp))
+            .background(gradient)
+            .clickable(
+                enabled = !isGenerating,
+                interactionSource = interactionSource,
+                indication = LocalIndication.current,
+                onClick = onClick
+            )
+            .padding(2.dp),
+        contentAlignment = Alignment.Center
+    ) {
+        Box(
+            modifier = Modifier
+                .fillMaxSize()
+                .clip(RoundedCornerShape(18.dp))
+                .background(FlashPlayPalette.Brand.copy(alpha = if (isGenerating) 0.78f else 0.92f)),
+            contentAlignment = Alignment.Center
+        ) {
+            if (isGenerating) {
+                Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(12.dp), verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically) {
+                    GalaxyMiniLoader()
+                    Text("Composing and saving locally", color = Color.White, fontWeight = FontWeight.Black, fontSize = 14.sp)
+                }
+            } else {
+                Text("Generate music", color = Color.White, fontWeight = FontWeight.Black, fontSize = 16.sp)
+            }
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+@Composable
+private fun GalaxyMiniLoader() {
+    val infinite = rememberInfiniteTransition(label = "mini-loader")
+    val phase by infinite.animateFloat(
+        initialValue = 0f,
+        targetValue = 1f,
+        animationSpec = infiniteRepeatable(animation = tween(780), repeatMode = RepeatMode.Restart),
+        label = "mini-loader-phase"
+    )
+    Row(
+        modifier = Modifier.size(width = 30.dp, height = 22.dp),
+        horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.SpaceBetween,
+        verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically
+    ) {
+        repeat(4) { index ->
+            val wave = kotlin.math.sin((phase * 360f + index * 55f) * Math.PI / 180f).toFloat()
+            Box(
+                modifier = Modifier
+                    .size(width = 4.dp, height = (10 + 8 * ((wave + 1f) / 2f)).dp)
+                    .clip(RoundedCornerShape(4.dp))
+                    .background(Color.White)
+            )
+        }
+    }
+}

- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.

- For sheets, slides, and documents, call `load_workspace_dependencies` to find the bundled runtime and libraries.
- If workspace dependencies are missing, call `install_workspace_dependencies` first.

### Automations
- This app supports recurring automations, reminders, monitors, follow-ups, and thread wakeups. When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

The `request_user_input` tool is unavailable in Default mode. If you call it while in Default mode, it will return an error.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions. - In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, call `load_workspace_dependencies` to find the bundled runtime and libraries.
- If workspace dependencies are missing, call `install_workspace_dependencies` first.

### Automations
- This app supports recurring automations, reminders, monitors, follow-ups, and thread wakeups. When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

The `request_user_input` tool is unavailable in Default mode. If you call it while in Default mode, it will return an error.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions. Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.

payload.developer_instructions:
<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, call `load_workspace_dependencies` to find the bundled runtime and libraries.
- If workspace dependencies are missing, call `install_workspace_dependencies` first.

### Automations
- This app supports recurring automations, reminders, monitors, follow-ups, and thread wakeups. When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.
- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}
</app-context>

# Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

The `request_user_input` tool is unavailable in Default mode. If you call it while in Default mode, it will return an error.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions. If you absolutely must ask a question because the answer cannot be discovered from local context and a reasonable assumption would be risky, ask the user directly with a concise plain-text question. Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.

<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, call `load_workspace_dependencies` to find the bundled runtime and libraries.
- If workspace dependencies are missing, call `install_workspace_dependencies` first.

### Automations
- This app supports recurring automations, reminders, monitors, follow-ups, and thread wakeups. When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.
- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}
</app-context>

name: Product Manager
description: Build products users love with discovery, prioritization, roadmapping, and cross-functional leadership.
metadata: {"clawdbot":{"emoji":"🎯","os":["linux","darwin","win32"]}}
---

# Product Management Rules

## Discovery
- Talk to users weekly — not just at project kickoff
- Watch behavior, don't just collect opinions — users say one thing, do another
- Problem validation before solution validation — are we solving the right thing?
- Jobs to be done: what's the user trying to accomplish?
- Competitors show what's possible, not what to copy

## Prioritization
- Impact vs effort is a starting point, not the answer
- Say no more than yes — focus is a feature
- Urgent vs important: stakeholder pressure isn't priority
- Stack rank ruthlessly — "everything is P1" means nothing is
- Revisit priorities when context changes — quarterly at minimum

## Roadmapping
- Outcomes over outputs — what will change, not what we'll build
- Time horizons: now (committed), next (planned), later (possible)
- Communicate uncertainty honestly — roadmaps aren't promises
- Dependencies surfaced early — blocked work wastes everyone's time
- Update when reality changes — stale roadmaps destroy trust

## Requirements
- User stories: who, what, why — not how
- Acceptance criteria define done — ambiguity creates rework
- Edge cases addressed upfront — not discovered in QA
- Scope creep is the enemy — good enough now beats perfect later
- Technical constraints are real — work with engineering, not around them

## Working with Engineering
- Context over directives — explain why, not just what
- Tradeoffs are collaborative decisions
- Spec before sprint, not during — no designing on the fly
- Protect focus time — meetings kill flow
- Trust their estimates, push back on scope not time

## Working with Design
- Research together, don't hand off briefs
- Critique the work, not the designer
- Design reviews with users, not just stakeholders
- Mobile and edge cases early — not afterthoughts
- Design system enables speed — support it

## Stakeholder Management
- Regular updates prevent surprise requests
- Data calms opinion battles
- Explain trade-offs, don't just defend decisions
- Feedback channels prevent end-runs — make input easy
- Executive sponsors for big initiatives

## Metrics
- One north star metric, 2-3 supporting
- Leading indicators for early signal — don't wait for lagging
- Dashboards should prompt questions, not just display numbers
- Vanity metrics feel good, don't drive decisions
- A/B test when data beats intuition

## Launch
- Soft launch catches problems before scale
- Success criteria defined before launch — not after
- Rollback plan before rollout
- Cross-functional checklist: docs, support, marketing
- Post-launch review: what worked, what didn't

## Common Mistakes
- Feature factory: shipping without learning
- Overspeccing: killing engineering autonomy
- Consensus seeking: decisions by committee
- Ignoring qualitative: data alone misses why
- Roadmap as backlog: detail everything, commit nothing

name: product-strategy
description: "Product strategy analysis for any consumer product. Competitive analysis, market sizing (TAM/SAM/SOM), pricing strategy, launch readiness assessment, and positioning. Built from 20 years of PM experience across consumer electronics, gaming, and mobile."
---

# Product Strategy Analyst

You are a senior product strategy analyst with 20 years of experience shipping consumer products. You provide specific, opinionated analysis grounded in frameworks and real market dynamics. You do not give generic PM advice. You give the kind of analysis that changes a decision.

## How You Work

When asked to analyze a product, market, or strategy question:

1. **Clarify scope first.** Ask what specific decision the analysis should inform. "Competitive analysis" means different things for a pitch deck vs a product roadmap vs a pricing decision.
2. **Use frameworks, but do not be a slave to them.** Reference the frameworks in your knowledge base, but adapt them to the specific situation. A TAM/SAM/SOM for a B2C hardware product looks different than one for a SaaS tool.
3. **End every section with "so what?"** Every observation must connect to a strategic implication. A feature comparison without insight is a spreadsheet, not analysis.
4. **Be opinionated.** State what you would do and why. "It depends" is not an answer. If it genuinely depends, name the 2-3 scenarios and what you would do in each.
5. **Name what you do not know.** If the analysis requires data you do not have, say so explicitly. Do not fill gaps with speculation.

## Commands

- `/analyze [product or category]` - Quick competitive landscape assessment. Key players, positioning map, gaps, and one strategic recommendation.
- `/market-size [market description]` - TAM/SAM/SOM estimation with methodology. Top-down and bottom-up triangulation. Caveats on data quality.
- `/pricing [product description]` - Pricing strategy recommendation. Competitive reference points, value-based anchoring, tier architecture, launch vs mature pricing.
- `/launch-check [product description]` - Launch readiness assessment against 6 dimensions. Red/yellow/green for each. Kill criteria evaluation.
- `/position [product description]` - Positioning statement generation with competitive frame, category strategy, and message testing approach.

## What You Read

Load relevant knowledge base files from your `references/` directory based on the command:

- `/analyze` -> `competitive-analysis.md`, `pm-heuristics.md`
- `/market-size` -> `market-sizing.md`
- `/pricing` -> `pricing-strategy.md`
- `/launch-check` -> `launch-readiness.md`, `pm-heuristics.md`
- `/position` -> `positioning.md`, `competitive-analysis.md`

If the user asks a broader strategy question that spans multiple workflows, combine the relevant reference files and keep the output oriented around the decision being made.

payload.message:
我调用并参考了 `/Users/vincet/.openclaw/workspace/skills/product-manager/SKILL.md` 的 PM 规则来分析。结论：MusePlay 现在功能方向对，但交互还像“功能集合”，需要更像“AI 音乐体验闭环”。

**核心问题**
用户的主要 Job 应该是：表达情绪或场景 → 快速得到适合自己的音乐 → 立即播放/收藏/再生成变体。  
现在 Listen、Create、Agent、Library 四个模块都有了，但用户旅程还断：Agent 的情绪理解、Create 的生成、Listen 的消费 feed 没有完全串起来。

**最高优先级改进**

1. **Create 生成前缺少明确预期**
现在用户填写 prompt 后点击生成，但不知道会等多久、生成什么类型、失败后怎么办。  
建议增加：预计耗时、当前步骤文案，例如 `Understanding mood / Composing / Saving locally`，进度条分阶段而不是单纯百分比。

2. **Agent 和生成音乐没有形成强闭环**
Agent 可以聊天和推荐，但它应该是产品灵魂。  
建议：Agent 对话后直接出现 2-3 个“一键生成”音乐卡片，例如 `安慰我 / 帮我提神 / 让我平静`。用户不应该再手动去 Create 填 prompt。

3. **Listen feed 的右侧按钮太少也太弱**
你要求只保留收藏和音量是对的，但缺少一个 AI 音乐 app 的关键动作：`生成相似` 或 `用这个感觉再来一首`。  
建议不放在右侧，可以放在底部标题附近做一个极简按钮：`Remix`。这是提高生成次数和留存的核心入口。

4. **默认播放体验需要更可靠**
用户已经多次反馈“没声音”。这是 P0 体验风险。  
建议在 app 内加一个首次播放检查：音量为 0、模拟器/设备静音、播放失败时，显示极简 toast 或底部提示：`Audio route unavailable` / `Tap to retry playback`。不要让用户猜。

5. **Library 价值不足**
Library 现在像列表，不像用户的个人音乐空间。  
建议分成三个轻量区：`Generated`、`Favorites`、`Mood History`。尤其 Mood History 可以把 Agent 情绪对话和生成音乐绑定起来。

**中优先级改进**

1. **生成失败恢复**
失败后应该保留用户输入，并提供 `Retry`、`Switch to instrumental`、`Random prompt` 三个恢复动作。现在错误只是提示，行动不够明确。

2. **Prompt 随机很好，但缺少“为什么适合我”**
每次进入 Create 随机 prompt 会有新鲜感，但用户可能迷失。  
建议显示一个很短的 mood tag，比如 `calm night`、`bright run`、`soft healing`，让随机不是随机噪音。

3. **Feed 动画要和音乐状态绑定**
Lottie/Canvas 动画不只是装饰，应该播放时更活跃、暂停时静止或变慢、切歌时有过渡。这样用户能直观看到“音乐活着”。

4. **收藏之后缺少反馈**
点击收藏应有非常轻的状态反馈：按钮弹一下、短文本 `Saved`，并确保 Library 里立刻可见。

5. **底部 Tab 命名可以更产品化**
`Listen / Create / Agent / Library` 清楚，但 Agent 如果是核心，可以考虑改成 `Muse` 或 `Mood`，更像超级音乐 app，而不是工具页。

**建议路线图**
Now：修播放可靠性、Create 分阶段进度、Agent 一键生成卡片、失败恢复。  
Next：Feed 增加 Remix、Library 情绪历史、动画绑定播放状态。  
Later：个性化推荐、用户画像、每日情绪音乐流、社交/分享。

我会把第一轮产品优化的优先级定为：**让 Agent 成为入口，让 Feed 成为消费，让 Remix 成为循环**。这是最有可能把 app 从“能生成音乐”推进到“让用户持续想玩”的交互骨架。

@Composable
private fun BottomBar(
    selectedTab: FlashTab,
    onSelect: (FlashTab) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier
) {
    Row(
        modifier = modifier
            .fillMaxWidth()
            .windowInsetsPadding(WindowInsets.navigationBars)
            .padding(horizontal = 18.dp, vertical = 6.dp)
            .clip(RoundedCornerShape(24.dp))
            .background(Color.White.copy(alpha = 0.96f))
            .padding(horizontal = 8.dp, vertical = 8.dp),
        horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp)
    ) {
        FlashTab.entries.forEach { tab ->
            val selected = tab == selectedTab
            val interactionSource = remember { MutableInteractionSource() }
            val pressed by interactionSource.collectIsPressedAsState()
            val scale by animateFloatAsState(
                targetValue = when {
                    pressed -> 0.96f
                    selected -> 1.04f
                    else -> 1f
                },
                animationSpec = spring(stiffness = Spring.StiffnessMediumLow, dampingRatio = Spring.DampingRatioMediumBouncy),
                label = "tab-scale"
            )
            val background by animateColorAsState(
                targetValue = if (selected) FlashPlayPalette.Brand else Color.Transparent,
                animationSpec = tween(180),
                label = "tab-bg"
            )
            val contentColor by animateColorAsState(
                targetValue = if (selected) Color.White else FlashPlayPalette.Ink,
                animationSpec = tween(180),
                label = "tab-color"
            )
            Box(
                modifier = Modifier
                    .weight(1f)
                    .graphicsLayer {
                        scaleX = scale
                        scaleY = scale
                    }
                    .clip(RoundedCornerShape(18.dp))
                    .background(background)
                    .clickable(
                        interactionSource = interactionSource,
                        indication = LocalIndication.current
                    ) { onSelect(tab) }

# Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

The `request_user_input` tool is unavailable in Default mode. If you call it while in Default mode, it will return an error.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions. If you absolutely must ask a question because the answer cannot be discovered from local context and a reasonable assumption would be risky, ask the user directly with a concise plain-text question. Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.

payload.developer_instructions:
<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, call `load_workspace_dependencies` to find the bundled runtime and libraries.
- If workspace dependencies are missing, call `install_workspace_dependencies` first.

### Automations
- This app supports recurring automations, reminders, monitors, follow-ups, and thread wakeups. When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.
- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}
</app-context>

- `→` 顺序播放
- `⤨` 随机播放
- `↻` 单曲循环

# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, call `load_workspace_dependencies` to find the bundled runtime and libraries.
- If workspace dependencies are missing, call `install_workspace_dependencies` first.

### Automations
- This app supports recurring automations, reminders, monitors, follow-ups, and thread wakeups. When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.
- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}
</app-context>
